flip.goal: I close every Transportation request in Boston on time in 2025.
flip.inverted: On December 31, 2025, I failed to close every Transportation request on time, just as in 2024, when 4,302 Parking Enforcement requests in South Boston / South Boston Waterfront went late, contributing to a staggering backlog.

hypothesis.name: Parking Enforcement backlog in South Boston
hypothesis.suspected_cause: Increased demand for parking enforcement during peak months without adequate staffing.

evidence.detail: 11,295 requests in South Boston / South Boston Waterfront; 4,302 overdue (38% vs 50% for the department), 2,043 past the 30-day cliff; modeled cost $290,340.

hypothesis.name: Capacity issues in peak months
hypothesis.suspected_cause: Insufficient crew availability to meet the high volume of requests during the busiest months.

evidence.detail: 17,836 requests citywide in months [5, 9, 10]; 10,081 overdue (57% vs 50% for the department), 3,080 past the 30-day cliff; modeled cost $509,620.

hypothesis.name: Silence from South Boston residents
hypothesis.suspected_cause: Residents under-reporting parking issues, leading to an incomplete understanding of demand.

evidence.detail: Residents in South Boston / South Boston Waterfront report at 0.76x the city rate for the same problem types (quietest: Recycling Cart Return at 0.53x).

hypothesis.name: Parking Enforcement backlog in Dorchester
hypothesis.suspected_cause: Continued high volume of late requests due to unaddressed enforcement needs.

evidence.detail: 6,840 requests in Dorchester; 3,609 overdue (53% vs 50% for the department), 1,639 past the 30-day cliff; modeled cost $236,080.

hypothesis.name: Parking Enforcement backlog in East Boston
hypothesis.suspected_cause: High volume of late requests due to lack of timely responses.

evidence.detail: 5,518 requests in East Boston; 3,108 overdue (56% vs 50% for the department), 1,345 past the 30-day cliff; modeled cost $196,660.

hypothesis.name: Parking Enforcement backlog in Jamaica Plain
hypothesis.suspected_cause: Persistent delays in addressing parking enforcement requests.

evidence.detail: 3,966 requests in Jamaica Plain; 2,620 overdue (66% vs 50% for the department), 1,149 past the 30-day cliff; modeled cost $167,300.

hypothesis.name: Parking Enforcement backlog in South End
hypothesis.suspected_cause: Failure to address the growing number of late requests in the neighborhood.

evidence.detail: 3,813 requests in South End; 2,100 overdue (55% vs 50% for the department), 1,024 past the 30-day cliff; modeled cost $144,400.
